source.title: The average size of a connected vertex set of a graph-Explicit formulas and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let P_n be the path on n vertices, let P_n x P_n be the Cartesian-product grid graph, and for any connected finite graph G define a connected set to be a vertex subset whose induced subgraph is connected. Let N(G) be the number of connected sets, S(G) the sum of their cardinalities, A(G)=S(G)/N(G), and D(G)=A(G)/|V(G)|. What is the limit of D(P_n x P_n) as n tends to infinity?

accepted.question_text: For every simple connected graph G of order n, let a_k be the number of connected vertex subsets of G with cardinality k, for k=0,1,2,...,n. Must the sequence (a_0,a_1,...,a_n) always be unimodal, meaning that it never increases again after it has begun to decrease?

accepted.question_text: For a graph G of order n, let c(G)=N(G)/2^n, where N(G) is the number of connected vertex subsets of G; this normalized count is at most 1 and measures how connected G is. Among simple connected 3-regular graphs, determine c_3, the limiting supremum of c(G). Which graph families, possibly including expander graphs, realize or improve lower bounds for this limiting supremum?

accepted.question_text: For connected finite graphs of order n, with D(G)=A(G)/n denoting the average size of a connected vertex set divided by n, is the path P_n the graph that minimizes D(G) among all graphs of order n?

accepted.question_text: For every connected finite graph G in which every vertex has degree at least 3, is the connected-set density D(G)=A(G)/|V(G)| always at least 1/2, where A(G) is the average cardinality of a connected vertex subset of G?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist connected finite graphs whose minimum degree is at least 3 and whose connected-set density D(G)=A(G)/|V(G)| is arbitrarily close to 1? Equivalently, determine whether the supremum of connected-set density over minimum-degree-at-least-3 graphs is 1, and if not, how far above the known necklace-family density 5/6 it can be pushed.
accepted.context_brief: High density with minimum degree at least three

evidence.quote: Question 8. Do there exist graphs with minimum degree at least 3 and density arbitrarily close to 1?
The necklaces Qn have a reasonable number of large separating sets, and the density is 5/6. By how much can this be increased?

trace.notes: Normalized the input URL as a zbMATH resolver with trailing identifier 7744491. Local resolver metadata in outputs/open-problems-0418-all.csv identified the exact work title and DOI 10.1002/jgt.22643.

The zbMATH landing URL itself did not expose readable full text through the available page reader. Bounded exact-work recovery by title and DOI found the author-hosted PDF at the University of Florida, whose first page matches the exact title and DOI. Local curl download of that PDF failed because the shell could not resolve people.clas.ufl.edu, so the web PDF text was used as the readable primary artifact.

Mapped the PDF section structure: Introduction, Previous Results, Two More Examples, Ladders-A Graph Theoretic Matrix Approach, Pell-number identities, Formulas for Ladders, Circular Ladders, Open Problems, and References. Definitions for connected set, N(G), S(G), A(G), and D(G) were taken from the introduction; all candidate open questions were concentrated in Section 8.
Extracted the explicit items labeled Question 1 through Question 5, Conjecture 6, Conjecture 7, and Question 8 from Section 8. No item was labeled solved or explicitly resolved in the source.
Expanded the grid-density question with the definitions of connected set, N(G), S(G), A(G), D(G), P_n, and Cartesian product from the introduction.
Rewrote the grid enumeration question so that N(P_n x P_n) and the n by n grid are defined without relying on prior notation.
Rewrote the n-cube enumeration question by spelling out the n-fold Cartesian product of P_2 and the meaning of N(G).
Expanded the unimodality question by defining a_k as the number of connected vertex subsets of each cardinality and stating the unimodality condition in words.
Combined Question 5 with its immediately following subquestions about families and expanders because they ask for the same limiting connectedness constant for simple connected 3-regular graphs.
Expanded the path-minimizer conjecture by restating density D(G) in terms of the average connected-set size divided by graph order.
Expanded the minimum-degree-three lower-bound conjecture with the definition of connected-set density and average connected-set size.
Expanded the upper-bound question by including the source's follow-up observation that necklace graphs have density 5/6 and asking how much this can be increased.
No near-duplicate items were merged. The follow-up about increasing necklace density was kept inside q_008 because it is part of the same upper-bound problem.

All eight accepted items have solved-status metadata set to false, page-number evidence, and self-contained rewrites. No candidates failed the evidence, self-containedness, no-new-facts, or schema gates.
Saved exact JSON result to outputs/parse-paper/7744491.json and outputs/latest.json.
